newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa shares rise on Australian profit contribution.
newsitem.headline: Axa shares rise on Australian profit contribution.

text.p: French insurer Axa announced on Friday its Australian unit National Mutual would kick in 291 million francs ($55.5 million) to its 1996 net profits, more than double its contribution for 1995.
"This compares very favourably with the pro forma contribution for 1995, which amounted to 125 million," said Axa, which acquired control of National Mutual in September 1995.
Axa reported profits of 2.73 billion francs in 1995.
Axa outperformed the Paris Bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index of 40 leading stocks on the back of the news.
By mid-afternoon, Axa shares were up 1.44 percent at 330.70 francs, outpacing the CAC-40 index which was up 0.88 percent.

Axa, which is merging with French rival Union des Assurances de Paris this year to create the world's second largest insurance group, said the improvement was partly driven by cost-cutting and business growth in Hong Kong.
Other factors it cited were favourable financial markets in 1996 and positive currency fluctuations.
Axa, which holds 51 percent of National Mutual, said the actual contribution for 1995, consolidated for one month only, was three million francs.
National Mutual reported last month that consolidated net income nearly doubled to A$210.9 million for its full year to September 30, 1996, from A$115.5 million a year earlier.

Fast-growing Axa, regarded as the most go-getting of French insurers, had said its A$1.1 billion takeover of National Mutual would give it a big headstart in Asia, the world's fastest growing insurance market.
But industry analysts have said National Mutual's expense levels are still a long way from meeting industry benchmarks.

National Mutual was forced into the arms of Axa, partly because of stricter Australian solvency rules due to go into effect this year and over-rapid expansion in the late 1980s which led to financial pressures. ($ = 5.239 French Francs)
